minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  January 29, 2019
1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by Mayor
  Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Don Kendrick, Mayor
  Robin Carder, Council Member
  Ernie Dorado, Resident
  Carolyn Cockrell, BUSD

  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Patti Latourelle, Resident
  Krista Chakmak, Resident
  Denise Fisher, Resident
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  David McElwain, Resident
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Francisco Cambero, LVPD
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  David Yim, Tri-City
  Isela Moreno, Tri-City
  Bill Aguirre, City of La Verne
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  October & November minutes were not approved due to
  lack of a quorum.

4. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer (SRO) Frankie Cambero shared
  information on recent incidents occurring at the high
  school as well as the elementary school. One incident
  involved a parent discovering threats being posted on
  social media by a local youth against other youth.
  Through the review of the issue, the school and SRO
  Cambero were able to provide necessary mental health
  support to the person making the threats before it
  escalated. Officer Cambero reminded the group to
  address these types of discovered issues immediately in
  order to prevent them from growing into more significant
  issues.

  Parents have been supportive and receptive of
  information regarding vaping. It continues to be a
  prominent and reoccurring issue facing the community’s
  youth. The group is hopeful that the latest video will have
  a positive impact.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes January 29, 2019, page 2

5. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers with the Bonita Unified School District
  provided information on expanding mental health
  counseling in local schools. Mark noted that catching
  students in need of mental health services early will help
  the students be more successful and prevent larger
  problems from developing later on. The group discussed
  how students in need are referred for services and how to
  ensure that they are properly and expeditiously identified.

  Mark informed the group about previous classes for
  students involving alcohol and drug use prevention. Mark
  noted that the BUSD was reviewing the possibility of
  bringing this course back with a vaping component as well.
  Mark also reported on a planned Drug Identification
  Training for Educational Professionals being hosted by
  BUSD in March. This training will assist educators in
  identifying signs of being under the influence and
  associated symptomology.

6. School Counseling Program  David Yim with Tri-City Mental Health Services reported
  that there have not been any significant changes from
  previous reports. November and December naturally have
  less activity due to the holiday season. David clarified the
  referral process and the need for parents to approve
  treatment. Some issues are more appropriately handled
  by the school counseling staff and not by Tri-City staff.

7. Mentor Program  Carolyn Cockrell from Roynon Elementary School spoke
  regarding the mentor program. Carolyn noted that last
  semester had 18 participants and that they are now
  making preparations for the new semester.

8. Vape Video  JR Ranells from the City of La Verne shared the draft vape
  video with the group. JR was provided with suggested
  changes and comments to be incorporated in the final
  video. Once the changes are made, the video will be
  finalized and posted on various social media platforms.

9. Round Table  SRO Cambero shared his desire to expand his and others
  knowledge through conversation.

  Hollie Savage inquired if the BUSD was doing any
  monitoring of social media sites. Mark informed the group
  that there is no formal monitoring in place.

  Sam Gonzalez provided follow up on YFAC fundraiser
  associated to the end of the NFL season. Sam shared
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes January 29, 2019, page 3

  some of the local winners and the positive impact of the
  program.

  Bill Aguirre provided the homeless count results and PD
  efforts for programs. Bill noted that there were increases
  from last year. The group discussed homelessness issues
  and programs available.

  Isela Moreno spoke about the upcoming stakeholders
  meeting.

  Resident David McElwain noted his connection to the Los
  Angeles County program that assists low income parents
  in finding employment. David also shared information on
  the Little Free Library program & benefits. Additionally,
  David informed the group on the Welcome Your Neighbor
  program started by the Mennonite Church as well as a Re-
  Entry/Records Expungement opportunity hosted by Los
  Angeles County taking place March 22nd.

  Greg Noyes from Ramona Middle School commented on
  Ramona having a great year.

  Krista Chakmak shared her interest in the community and
  schools.

  Council Member Robin Carder stated she appreciated the
  Police Department for all the wonderful things they do for
  the community.

10.  Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for March 26, 2019
  at 6:30 p.m.

11. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 8:20 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Personnel Officer
